geography: Late Jurassic lithographic limestones of Bavaria, Germany
overview: A Late Jurassic avialan known from a small Bavarian specimen series; it lies outside crown Neornithes and is not presented as the direct ancestor of living birds.

ecology.diet: Not resolved by the cited flight and systematic studies
ecology.habitat: Solnhofen-archipelago carbonate environments represented by Bavarian lithographic limestones
ecology.locomotion: Terrestrial and aerial capacities; flight style is inferred from bone geometry rather than observed behaviour
ecology.guild: Unresolved; no single feeding guild is assigned from the cited evidence

traits: Asymmetrical flight feathers associated with skeletal specimens
Toothed jaws and a long bony tail
Pectoral geometry compatible with short-burst active flight in a biomechanical comparison
evidenceSummary: The oldest referred specimen extends the genus into the earliest Tithonian Painten Formation and documents substantial anatomical variation; synchrotron comparisons support active flight capacity but not modern crown-bird flight performance.

geography: Antarctica and Europe for the two Maastrichtian fossil tests highlighted here
overview: The crown group defined by the common ancestor of living birds and all descendants; this boundary excludes Archaeopteryx and keeps Cretaceous fossil membership tied to explicit phylogenetic analyses.

ecology.diet: Highly diverse; the highlighted Vegavis skull supports underwater prey capture for that fossil only
ecology.habitat: Global across marine, freshwater and terrestrial environments today
ecology.locomotion: Predominantly volant, with multiple independently flight-reduced or flightless lineages

traits: Crown membership is defined relationally, not by one universally diagnostic fossil character
Vegavis skull anatomy combines an avian beak and crown-like neuroanatomy with a specialized feeding apparatus
Asteriornis preserves a different late Maastrichtian galloanseran character combination
evidenceSummary: A 2025 skull analysis strengthens crown-waterfowl placement for older Vegavis, but the study explicitly records its earlier contested placements; younger Asteriornis also shifts among near-crown positions under different analyses.

geography: Pekin Formation, Chatham County, North Carolina, United States
overview: A Carnian crocodylomorph represented here by partial, skeletally immature holotype NCSM 21558 and referred humerus NCSM 21623; its basal placement and predator-guild role are results of the cited analyses, not direct ancestry or behaviour.

ecology.diet: Faunivory is inferred from serrated, recurved teeth rather than directly observed feeding
ecology.habitat: Terrestrial Pekin Formation assemblage in the study's reconstruction
ecology.locomotion: Treated as terrestrial in the cited comparison; locomotor performance was not directly tested
ecology.bodySize: Approximately 3 m in the study's reconstruction, with an immature femur-length estimate of 353–440 mm
ecology.guild: Top-tier terrestrial predator in the sampled Pekin Formation assemblage, as interpreted by the study

traits: NCSM 21558 preserves parts of the skull, vertebral column, ribs and left humerus
The reconstructed skull is slender and ornamented, with an estimated length greater than 50 cm
Premaxillary teeth are elongate, serrated and slightly recurved
evidenceSummary: The holotype anatomy, Chatham County horizon and approximately 231 Ma age are direct specimen and geological records; total length, body-mass proxy, guild assignment and basal crocodylomorph placement remain bounded analytical interpretations.

overview: A latest Maastrichtian bird represented by CT-imaged holotype NHMM 2013 008; the original analyses place it near crown Galloanserae but disagree on its exact branch, so the profile does not use it as a universal crown-bird first appearance.

ecology.diet: Not resolved by the cited description
ecology.habitat: A possible littoral ecology inferred from the marine depositional context, not a directly observed habitat preference
ecology.locomotion: Not resolved by the cited description
ecology.bodySize: Mean body-mass estimate of 394 g from the study's skeletal scaling model
ecology.guild: No feeding or locomotor guild is assigned from the cited evidence

traits: A nearly complete, three-dimensionally preserved skull is associated with fragmentary postcranial elements
The skull combines galliform-like and anseriform-like features in the authors' comparison
Parsimony and tip-dated Bayesian analyses recover different near-galloanseran positions
evidenceSummary: NHMM 2013 008, the 66.8–66.7 Ma horizon, CT anatomy and 394 g model estimate are source-bounded; crown position, possible littoral ecology and biogeographic implications remain analysis-dependent.
